system.name: Conveyor
system.one_liner: a general-purpose continuous software deployment system built from stateless, worker-pool services that coordinate through a shared partitioned database

components.name: Conveyor Core
components.role: the group of stateless services centered on the shared database

components.name: Database
components.role: shared, sharded store of pipelines, metadata, and the last step executed for each release and action

components.name: Release Creator
components.role: periodically scans for new input artifacts and creates a release object when they are discovered

components.name: Artifact Finders
components.role: pluggable finders invoked to discover new input artifacts for a pipeline

components.name: Backend Artifact Finder
components.role: a standard finder for backend build artifacts

components.name: Mobile Artifact Finder
components.role: a standard finder for mobile build artifacts

components.name: Configuration Artifact Finder
components.role: a standard finder for configuration artifacts

components.name: Run Scheduler
components.role: periodically scans releases and steps through each action in a pipeline to schedule execution

components.name: Run Manager
components.role: initiates action execution, tracks progress, and records the outcome back to the database

components.name: Action Services
components.role: services implementing the logic of standard or custom pipeline actions

components.name: Deploy
components.role: standard action for deploying a new version to production

components.name: Build
components.role: standard action for compiling source code and running unit tests

content.key_idea: Conveyor's stateless services (Release Creator, Run Scheduler, Run Manager) coordinate purely through a shared partitioned database, discovering artifacts and executing pipeline actions via pluggable Artifact Finders and Action Services, following a numbered seven-step create-release/schedule/run-action cycle.
content.reading_order: Follow the seven circled numbers radiating from Conveyor Core: Release Creator and Artifact Finders on the left create releases (steps 1-3), then Run Scheduler and Run Manager on the right schedule and run actions via Action Services (steps 4-7).

summary: This figure depicts Conveyor's architecture as a set of stateless services coordinating through a shared, sharded Database inside Conveyor Core. On the create-release side, a Release Creator periodically scans state (step 1), invokes pluggable Artifact Finders such as Backend, Mobile and Configuration finders to discover new artifacts (step 2), and writes a new release object to the database to trigger the pipeline (step 3). On the run-action side, a Run Scheduler periodically scans releases and actions to decide what to run (step 4), notifies the Run Manager (step 5), which invokes the appropriate Action Service such as Deploy, Test or Build (step 6) and records the outcome back to the database (step 7). The diagram places Conveyor Core at the center with the other components as spokes, connected by curved arrows carrying circled step numbers 1 through 7, visually emphasizing that all coordination flows through the shared database rather than direct service-to-service calls.
summary_zh: Conveyor 架构：无状态服务经共享数据库协作，Release Creator 发现制品创建 release，Run Scheduler 调度、Run Manager 执行动作并写回结果，步骤编号 1-7。
